Document: Practice Direction 51R – Online Civil Money Claims Pilot
Part 4 of 10
==================================================
[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6C.3(1 ) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (4 ) As soon as practicable after the date that all trial readiness certificates are submitted, the court shall—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6C.3(1 ) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (a) fix the date for the trial, unless it has already done so;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6C.3(1 ) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (b) give any directions for the trial, including a trial timetable, which it considers appropriate; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6C.3(1 ) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (c) specify any further steps that need to be taken before trial,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6C.3(1 ) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] and the court shall give the parties at least 3 weeks’ notice of the date of the trial unless, in exceptional circumstances, the court directs that shorter notice be given. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6C.3(1 ) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (5)  Notwithstanding that the parties must complete a trial readiness certificate, a judge may nevertheless direct that a pre-trial checklist (listing questionnaire) be sent to the parties for completion as well. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6C.3(1 ) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (6) If a pre-trial checklist is sent to the parties for completion under subparagraph (5)–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6C.3(1 ) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (a) Civil Procedure Rule 28.4 applies with the following modification: rule 28.4(1) applies as if it permits (but does not require) the court to send the parties a pre-trial checklist (listing questionnaire) for completion and return in accordance with that rule;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6C.3(1 ) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (b) Civil Procedure Rules PD 28 paragraph 6.1(2) similarly applies as if it permits (but does not require) the court to send out Forms N170 and N171 to the parties; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6C.3(1 ) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (c) Civil Procedure Rule 28.5 applies. ## Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] 6C.3A(1) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to intermediate track or the multi-track. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (2) Civil Procedure Rule 28.4, 28.5, 29.6 and 29.7 do not apply, except to the extent provided for by subparagraph (4) and (5). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (3) A judge may direct that parties must complete and upload to the OCMC website a pre-trial checklist (listing questionnaire) – Form N170). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (4) If the claim is allocated to the intermediate track and a judge directs that the parties complete and upload a pre-trial checklist under subparagraph (3)–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (a) Civil Procedure Rule 28.4 applies with the following modification –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (i) rule 28.4 applies as if a reference to filing or returning includes filing or returning by uploading to the OCMC website;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (ii) rule 28.4(1) applies as if it permits (but does not require) a judge to direct that parties must complete and upload a pre-trial checklist (listing questionnaire) in accordance with that rule;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (iii) rule 28.4(3) applies as if, if no party uploads a pre-trial checklist by the date specified in the notice of allocation, the claim is to be referred to a judge for directions; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (iv) rule 28.4(4) applies as if a reference to the court is a reference to a judge;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (b) Civil Procedure Rules PD 28 paragraph 6.1 applies with the following modification –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (i) paragraph 6.1 applies as if a reference to filing includes filing or returning by uploading to the OCMC website; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (ii) paragraph 6.1(2) does not apply; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (c) Civil Procedure Rule 28.5 applies as if a reference to filing includes filing or returning by uploading to the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (5) If the claim is allocated to the multi-track and a pre-trial checklist is sent to the parties for completion under subparagraph (3)–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (a)  Civil  Procedure  Rule  29.6  as  appropriate  applies  with  the  following modification –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (i) rule 29.6 applies as if a reference to filing includes filing or returning by uploading to the OCMC website;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (ii) rule 29.6(1) applies as if it permits (but does not require) a judge to direct that the parties must complete and upload to the OCMC website a pre-trial checklist (listing questionnaire) – Form N170;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (iii) rule 29.6(3) applies as if, if no party uploads a pre-trial checklist by the date specified in the notice of allocation, the claim is to be referred to a judge for directions; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (iv) rule 29.6(4) applies as if a reference to the court is a reference to a judge;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (b) Civil Procedure Rules PD 29 paragraphs 8.1 to 8.4 similarly apply with the following modification –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (i)  paragraphs 8.1 to 8.4 apply as if a reference to filing includes filing by uploading to the OCMC website; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (ii) paragraph 8.1(4) does not apply;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (iii) paragraph 8.3(1) applies as if, if no party uploads a pre-trial checklist on time, the claim is to be referred to a judge for directions; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (c) Civil Procedure Rule 29.7 applies. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] (Civil Procedure Rules Practice Direction 28 paragraph 7.2 contains provisions in relation to trial bundles for claims in the intermediate track; Civil Procedure Rules Practice Direction 29 paragraph 9.2 contains provisions in relation to trial bundles for claims in the multi-track.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists] Claims allocated to the fast track – “trial bundles” (as defined )

## 6C.4(A1) This paragraph applies to claims allocated to the fast track. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6C.4(A1) This paragraph applies to claims allocated to the fast track.] 6C.4(1) Civil Procedure Rules PD28 paragraph 7.2(2)(c) shall have effect as if after “trial bundle” there were inserted “(but only if the parties consider this necessary, in the light of the automatic creation of a trial bundle in Online Civil Money Claims)”. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6C.4(A1) This paragraph applies to claims allocated to the fast track.] (2) Civil Procedure Rules PD28 paragraph 9.4 shall have effect as if after “base its order on those forms” there were inserted “, save that, in the light of the automatic creation of a trial bundle in Online Civil Money Claims, a direction for the lodging of a trial bundle should only be made if the court considers such a direction to be necessary. ## Claims allocated to the small claims track – “trial bundles” (as defined)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the small claims track – “trial bundles” (as defined)] 6C.5 Where the claim is allocated to the small claims track, when giving directions about preparation for the final hearing, the court is to consider including a direction that each party must, not less than 21 days before the date fixed for the final hearing, upload to the OCMC website copies of all documents (other than documents which already have been uploaded) which they wish the court to consider when reaching its decision. (The court will assemble the documents into a “trial bundle” (as defined)). (Civil Procedure Rules Part 27 contains further provisions about claims allocated to the small claims track, and Part 39 contains further rules about hearings, all of which apply to the extent they do not conflict with this practice direction.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the small claims track – “trial bundles” (as defined)] Sub-section A – Introduction to this Section

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the small claims track – “trial bundles” (as defined)] 7.1(1) Subject to sub-paragraph (1A), this Section applies where the defendant responds electronically admitting the whole or part of the claim, or admitting part and defending the rest of the claim. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the small claims track – “trial bundles” (as defined)] (1A) The provisions of this Section listed below apply as provided below—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the small claims track – “trial bundles” (as defined)] (a) paragraphs 7.8, 7.9, 7.41C and 7.41D only apply (as provided in sub-paragraph (1)(za) of each of those paragraphs) where none of the parties is represented by a legal representative;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the small claims track – “trial bundles” (as defined)] (b) paragraph 7.10 (and with it paragraphs 7.11-7.15) applies only where none of the parties is represented by a legal representative, except that (by virtue of paragraph 7.10(2A)) paragraph 7.10(2) applies where the claimant (but not the defendant) is, or all the parties are, represented by a legal representative, so as to provide that the claim is sent out of Online Civil Money Claims at that stage: and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the small claims track – “trial bundles” (as defined)] (c) paragraphs 7.2, 7.3, 7.37 and 7.38 also apply where the defendant (but not the claimant) is represented by a legal representative, and  by virtue of paragraph 7.3A (where the defendant admits the whole of the claim) or paragraph 7.38A (where the defendant admits part  of the claim and defends the rest of the claim) as appropriate,  provide that the claim is sent out of Online Civil Money Claims to  the CTSC (as defined) at that stage. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the small claims track – “trial bundles” (as defined)] (2) Sub-section B applies only to full admissions, where the defendant uses the response screens on the OCMC website to make the admission of the whole of the claim and makes no other response

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the small claims track – “trial bundles” (as defined)] (3) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the small claims track – “trial bundles” (as defined)] (4) Sub-section D applies where the defendant part admits the claim and defends the rest of it, and uses the response screens on the OCMC website to make the part admission and part defence. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the small claims track – “trial bundles” (as defined)] (5) Sub-section E applies to both full and part admissions, where the defendant uses the response screens on the OCMC website to make the admission and there has been a change of circumstances. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the small claims track – “trial bundles” (as defined)] (6) Sub-section F applies to both full and part admissions, where the defendant responds electronically, but does not use the response screens on the OCMC website to make the admission. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the small claims track – “trial bundles” (as defined)] (7) Sub-section G applies where –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the small claims track – “trial bundles” (as defined)] (a) the amount of the claim excluding interest is more than £25,000;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the small claims track – “trial bundles” (as defined)] (b) all the parties are represented by a legal representative;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Claims allocated to the small claims track – “trial bundles” (as defined)] (c) there is more than one defendant; and (d) the defendant’s responses differ from one another. ## Introduction to Sub-section B

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Introduction to Sub-section B] 7.2 This sub-section applies where the defendant admits the whole of the claim, and the defendant uses the response screens on the OCMC website to make the admission and makes no other response. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Introduction to Sub-section B] Court to notify the claimant where the defendant proposes to make payment of the whole amount

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Introduction to Sub-section B] 7.3 When the court tells the claimant that it has received the admission, it must also tell the claimant –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Introduction to Sub-section B] (a) whether the defendant has offered to pay the whole amount owed so that the claimant receives it within 5 days of the date of the admission, or whether the defendant has asked for more time to pay; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Introduction to Sub-section B] (b) if the defendant has asked for more time to pay, what “repayment plan” (as defined) the defendant is proposing for payment, which could be payment so that the claimant receives it by a date that is more than 5 days after the date of admission, or payment by instalments. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Introduction to Sub-section B] Court to send case out of Online Civil Money Claims following notification to the claimant made pursuant to paragraph 7.3 in certain circumstances

## 7.3A Where—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (a) the court has made a notification to the claimant pursuant to paragraph 7.3; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (b) the defendant (but not the claimant) is represented by a legal representative,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] the claim must be sent out of Online Civil Money Claims to the CTSC (as defined) at that stage. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] Defendant offers to pay the whole amount owed within 5 days

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] 7.4(1) If the defendant has offered to pay the whole amount so that the claimant receives it within 5 days of the date of the admission, but then the claimant does not receive the whole amount within that time, the claimant may request a judgment on admission. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (2) The claimant requests the judgment by completing form OCON225 and submitting it to the court using the OCMC website where none of the parties is represented by a legal representative, or if the claimant is, or all the parties are, legally represented, by the claimant requesting judgment using the relevant screens on the OCMC website. When requesting judgment, the claimant may also specify its repayment plan (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (3) If the court receives a request for judgment on admission, it must “enter judgment” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (4) If the claimant has specified a repayment plan in the request for judgment, the judgment must state that repayment is to be made in accordance with that repayment plan. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (5) If the claimant has not specified a repayment plan in the request for judgment, the judgment must state that the whole amount owed must be repaid in full immediately. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (6) The judgment will be made for the amount of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (a) the claim;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (b) any interest that the claimant is entitled to and has claimed on the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (c) court fees, and any fixed costs that the claimant is entitled to in accordance with Section 2B,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] minus any payments of the amount owed on the claim form that the defendant has already paid. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (If a claimant wants to claim any costs other than court fees, for example the costs of paying for expert evidence, the claimant would have to make an application. Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] Defendant has not offered to pay the amount owed within 5 days, but instead has asked for more time to pay and has proposed a repayment plan

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] 7.5(1) If the defendant has not offered to pay the amount owed so that the claimant receives it within 5 days of the date of the admission, but the defendant has instead asked for more time to pay and has proposed “a repayment plan” (as defined), the claimant may accept or reject the proposal. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (2) The claimant accepts or rejects the proposal by completing form OCON225 and submitting it to the court using the OCMC website where none of the parties is represented by a legal representative, or if the claimant is, or all the parties are, legally represented, by the claimant accepting or rejecting the proposal using the relevant screens on the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] Claimant accepts the defendant’s proposed repayment plan

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] 7.6(1) If the claimant has accepted the defendant’s proposed repayment plan using form OCON225 or using the relevant screens on the OCMC website (as appropriate), the claimant may request a judgment on admission, but does not have to: if none of the parties is represented by a legal representative, the claimant may decide to propose a settlement agreement instead. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] Claimant accepts defendant’s repayment plan and decides to request a judgment on admission

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] 7.7(1) If the claimant decides to request a judgment on admission, the claimant requests the judgment by completing form OCON225 and submitting it to the court using the OCMC website where none of the parties is represented by a legal representative, or if the claimant is, or all the parties are, legally represented, by the claimant requesting judgment using the relevant screens on the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (2) If the court receives a request for judgment on admission, it must “enter judgment” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (3) The judgment will be made for the amount of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (a) the claim;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (b) any interest that the claimant is entitled to and has claimed on the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (c) court fees, and any fixed costs that the claimant is entitled to in accordance with Section 2B,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] minus any payments of the amount owed on the claim form that the defendant has already paid. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (If a claimant wants to claim any costs other than court fees, for example the costs of paying for expert evidence, the claimant would have to make an application. Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (4) The judgment must state that the amount is to be paid in accordance with the defendant’s repayment plan unless, at the time the judgment is made, a repayment date specified in that repayment plan has passed. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (5) If a repayment date specified in the repayment plan has passed before the judgment is made, the judgment must still be made in accordance with that repayment plan, but –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (a) if the repayment plan states that the whole of the amount owed is to be paid by a date that has passed, the judgment must state that repayment must be made immediately;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] (b) if the repayment plan states that the amount owed is to be paid by instalments and the date of the first instalment has passed, the judgment must state that the first instalment must be made by a date that is one calendar month after the date of the judgment, and with subsequent instalments to be paid at one calendar month intervals after that. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3A Where—] Claimant accepts defendant’s proposed repayment plan, proposes a settlement agreement instead of requesting a judgment on admission – defendant accepts the proposal for a settlement agreement

## 7.8(1) If –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.8(1) If –] (za) none of the parties is represented by a legal representative;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.8(1) If –] (a)  instead of requesting a judgment on admission, the claimant has proposed a settlement agreement on the same terms as the defendant’s proposed repayment plan;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.8(1) If –] (b) the proposed agreement is in the form of OCON Settlement Agreement A;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.8(1) If –] (c) the claimant has used the OCMC website to notify the court of the proposal to the defendant; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.8(1) If –] (d) the defendant has, within 7 days of the date of the claimant’s proposal, used the OCMC website to notify the court that they have accepted the proposal and agree to the settlement agreement,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.8(1) If –] the court must “stay” the proceedings (as defined). When it stays the proceedings, the court must enable the claimant to return to court to request judgment on admission for any money still owed under the settlement agreement, if the settlement agreement breaks down, and the defendant fails to comply with the settlement agreement. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.8(1) If –] (2) If the settlement agreement breaks down, the claimant requests judgment on admission by completing form OCON225 and submitting it to the court using the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.8(1) If –] (3) If the court receives a request for judgment on admission, it must “enter judgment” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.8(1) If –] (4) The judgment will be made for the amount of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.8(1) If –] (a) the claim;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.8(1) If –] (b) any interest that the claimant is entitled to and has claimed on the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.8(1) If –] (c) court fees,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.8(1) If –] minus any payments of the amount owed on the claim form that the defendant has already paid. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.8(1) If –] (If a claimant wants to claim any costs other than court fees, for example the costs of paying for expert evidence, the claimant would have to make an application. Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.8(1) If –] (5) The judgment must state that the amount is to be paid in accordance with the terms of the settlement agreement , unless, at the time the judgment is made, a repayment date specified in the settlement agreement has passed. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.8(1) If –] (6) If a repayment date specified in the settlement agreement has passed before the judgment is made, the judgment must still be made in accordance with that settlement agreement, but –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.8(1) If –] (a) if the settlement agreement states that the whole of the amount owed is to be paid by a date that has passed, the judgment must state that repayment must be made immediately;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.8(1) If –] (b) if the settlement agreement states that the amount owed is to be paid by instalments and the date of the first instalment has passed, the judgment must state that the first instalment must be made by a date that is one calendar month after the date of the judgment, and with subsequent instalments to be paid at one calendar month intervals after that.
